Comments: No credible evidence found after searching birth registration refugees non-citizens

revision_notes: Original Unknown (0, no source) was not correct: UNHCR reporting confirms Cameroon's civil registration legislation (Ordinance No. 81/002 of 1981, amended by Law No. 2011/011, now superseded by Law No. 2024/016 of 23 December 2024) applies broadly and does not exclude non-citizens, and that specific programmes (World Bank-financed Social Safety Nets project, NRC legal/civil documentation support) actively register refugees and IDPs (mainly Central African Republic and Nigerian refugees, and Anglophone-crisis IDPs) for civil status events including birth certificates. Registration completion rates for these groups are low in practice, but non-citizens are not legally or programmatically excluded. Score raised from 0 to 3 (Some refugees and IDPs), short of universal/automatic inclusion (4).
revised_comments: Cameroon's civil registration system, governed by Law No. 2024/016 of 23 December 2024 (replacing the 1981 Ordinance as amended in 2011), applies to residents generally and does not bar refugees, asylum-seekers, or IDPs from registering vital events. In practice, refugees (predominantly from the Central African Republic and Nigeria) and IDPs are supported in accessing birth, death and marriage registration through targeted government and partner programmes, including the World Bank-financed Social Safety Nets Project and NRC legal and civil documentation assistance. Registration completion rates among these groups remain low, however, due to weak civil registration infrastructure in crisis-affected regions (Far North, North-West, South-West) and practical barriers to accessing registration centres.

Implementation is still maturing: as of late 2025, delays and complications in ID issuance and biometric voter card distribution mean the linkage between the ID and electoral systems functions but is not yet fully realised nationwide.
